mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS is below 3.0% (the 20th percentile of historical values), or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of triggered instances (UNRATE > 5.0%), or the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production and housing starts indicates a broad-based economic contraction, reducing corporate investment and earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where both INDPRO and HOUST decline by more than 0.5% in the prior month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising > 0.25 percentage points in three months), the S&P 500 produces negative returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced liquidity and higher discount rates.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of triggered instances (FEDFUNDS rising > 0.25pp in 3 months), or the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of housing starts indicates strong consumer demand for residential construction, boosting economic activity and corporate earnings, which leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where HOUST is above the 80th percentile of historical values, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A consumer price inflation rate exceeding 3.0% signals rising inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of triggered instances (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%), or the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in employment growth (PAYEMS) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) signals a deteriorating labor market, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises by more than 0.2pp in the prior month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a labor market recovery (UNRATE falling below 5.0% and PAYEMS rising by more than 50,000 in three months), the S&P 500 produces positive returns over the next 60 trading days due to improved consumer spending and corporate earnings growth.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5.0% and PAYEMS rises > 50k in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of triggered instances (UNRATE < 5.0% and PAYEMS rising > 50k in 3 months), or the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
